title: Tacos al Pastor
subtitle: Mexican spit-roasted pork tacos with pineapple
excerpt: Mexico's most beloved taco: pork marinated in dried chillies, achiote, and pineapple juice, cooked until caramelised, and served in small corn tortillas with pineapple, coriander, and raw onion. The marinade comes from the Lebanese shawarma tradition brought to Mexico.

recipe.sourceNotes: Tacos al pastor (shepherd-style tacos) derive from shawarma, brought to Mexico by Lebanese immigrants in the early twentieth century who settled primarily in Puebla. The Mexican adaptation replaced the lamb of the original with pork, swapped the Middle Eastern spices for Mexican dried chillies and achiote (annatto seed paste), and added pineapple. The vertical spit on which the meat is cooked (trompo) is directly descended from the shawarma spit. In Mexico City al pastor taco stands are open until the small hours and are the essential late-night eating. At home, the pork is most commonly marinated and cooked in a griddle or cast-iron pan at high heat, which mimics the caramelised edges produced by the spit.

content.text: Marinate the pork for at least 4 hours; overnight gives a more intense result. The pork should be sliced very thin (about 3 mm) so it cooks quickly and develops caramelised edges on a hot griddle. The pineapple is added to the pan at the very end and heated only briefly to soften slightly and pick up colour.

items.preparation: pork shoulder preferred; sliced 3 mm thin against the grain
dried ancho or guajillo chillies; soaked in hot water for 20 minutes, then blended
fresh; cut into chunks; to add at the end of cooking
very finely diced; raw; to serve

content.text: Blend the soaked chillies with the garlic, vinegar, paprika, cumin, oregano, sugar, and salt to a smooth paste. Toss the pork slices in the marinade. Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours.

Heat a large cast-iron pan or griddle over the highest possible heat. Add a little oil. Cook the pork slices in batches, without moving, for 2 to 3 minutes per side until charred at the edges and cooked through. Transfer to a board and roughly chop.

Add 150 g fresh pineapple chunks to the hot pan for 1 minute until lightly charred. Warm small corn tortillas directly over a gas flame or in a dry pan. Fill each tortilla with pork and pineapple, then top with raw diced onion and fresh coriander. Serve with lime wedges.
